equity_bridge.note: H1 FY2026 condensed balance sheet; flows are consolidated so the NCI stock is deducted once here

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Management medium-term guidance (mid-single-digit underlying sales CAGR) cross-checked against delivered underlying growth of 5%/3%/4% in FY2023-25 and 4% in H1 FY2026; the headline GBP CAGRs are not usable (see warning)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-6.1% 3yr) diverges by far more than 30% from EPS (+15.9%) and revenue (-2.3%): equity shrinks because GBP1.7bn has been returned via buybacks since 2020 and USD weakness drives translation losses, not because the business is shrinking. Headline revenue CAGRs are depressed by the FY2022-23 disposals (international courseware local publishing, Pearson Online Learning Services) and the FY2025 USD move. The equity CAGR is therefore rejected as a growth anchor in favour of underlying sales growth.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - lease principal; IAS 17 years pre-FY2019 have no lease deduction): FY2019 60, FY2020 134, FY2021 34, FY2022 86, FY2023 275, FY2024 381, FY2025 406 (ex the GBP97m tax refund c.309). Owner-FCF CAGRs exceed reported-FCF CAGRs because SBC (c.1% of sales) and lease principal (c.GBP80m) are near-fixed deductions off a rising base -- the opposite of the SBC-outgrowing-cash-flow pattern. All FCF CAGRs are measured from the FY2020-22 trough (COVID assessment disruption, portfolio reshaping) and overstate the sustainable rate; they are reported, not used.

scenario_narratives.base: Pearson delivers its medium-term framework roughly as guided: mid-single-digit underlying sales growth (c.4% in GBP after USD translation), +40bps/yr of margin from operating leverage, cost efficiency and the holding-company-to-operating-company simplification, and 90-100% free-cash conversion. Assessment & Qualifications (45% of sales, 59% of profit) remains the anchor -- contract renewals, pricing and the new AI-skills certification work through Pearson VUE -- while Virtual Learning compounds enrolments, Higher Education grows low-single-digit on Inclusive Access and pricing, and English Language Learning is a drag until PTE stabilises. Cash is returned through a 5%-growing dividend and c.GBP350m/yr buybacks, which are value-neutral in this model. The 22 Oct 2026 nine-month update is the first checkpoint; a cut to the GBP640-685m profit range would move year 1.
scenario_narratives.bull: AI turns out to be a demand driver for Pearson rather than a substitute: the certification agreement with a leading AI lab is the first of several enterprise-scale skills-verification programmes delivered through the VUE test-centre network, Enterprise Learning & Skills becomes a genuine third growth vector, Virtual Learning sustains high-single-digit enrolment growth, HE's platform convergence lifts US courseware share, and PTE recovers as migration flows normalise. Underlying growth runs 5-5.5% for five years and margins expand c.60bps/yr to a 20%+ adjusted operating margin by 2030 while capex intensity eases. Unmodelled upside on top: the c.GBP480m UK pension surplus (c.60p/share after refund tax) and any Anthropic class-action distribution.
scenario_narratives.bear: Generative AI answer engines and free AI tutors hollow out Higher Education courseware and study-tool pricing faster than Pearson can reposition; PTE's decline proves structural as the UK, Australia and Canada keep tightening study-visa routes; a major US state assessment contract is lost on renewal and US K12 virtual-school funding tightens; and USD weakness compounds the GBP numbers. Group growth stalls at c.1%, margins give back c.120bps because Pearson must keep spending c.12% of sales on product and AI to defend its position, and the market re-rates it to a 12x cash multiple. There is no balance-sheet stress in this path (net debt/EBITDA stays well under the 2x self-imposed cap); the loss is a permanently lower earnings base, not solvency.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Pearson is valued as a mature, cash-generative operating company on an owner-FCF basis: SBC expensed and the share count held flat, lease cash charged inside the flows with lease liabilities out of net debt, capitalised product development treated as the capex it is, and the FY2025 tax refund and working-capital swing both normalised away. The business is c.90% operationally complex assessment, virtual-school and print services with high renewal rates, which supports the medium-term framework in the base case; the valuation question is whether AI expands demand for trusted skills verification (bull) or erodes courseware economics (bear). Value is mostly terminal (a 2% perpetuity on a 34% EBITDA / c.13% owner-FCF margin, capped at 15x), discounted at a GBP WACC of 8% used identically across scenarios so that risk is charged once, in the probability-weighted flows.
key_risks_to_valuation: Generative AI substituting Higher Education courseware, study tools and English-language instruction; the bull/bear spread is largely this axis
PTE (English test) volumes tied to UK/Australia/Canada migration and study-visa policy; already declining in H1 FY2026
US state and national assessment contract renewals in A&Q (45% of sales, 59% of profit); a single large loss moves the group
USD translation: c.60% of revenue in USD, guidance set at GBP:USD 1.35, 1c = c.GBP5m adjusted operating profit
Capitalised product development (c.8% of sales) running above amortisation would mean reported FCF conversion overstates economic cash generation; the model charges the cash
US K12 virtual-school funding and charter authorisations (Virtual Learning, 14% of sales)
Rising net debt from debt-funded buybacks (GBP1.4bn at 30 Jun 2026, 1.3x adjusted EBITDA) if cash flow disappoints; adjusted net finance costs guided to c.GBP80m
Terminal value is c.55% of EV; each 0.5pt of WACC is worth roughly 7-8% of base value

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 874.8-1337.0 GBp
data_sources.financials: PSON.L_Metrics.csv (core_metrics, FY2014-FY2025 plus H1 FY2024-26); FY2025 Annual Report (cash flow statement, note 7 EPS dilution, adjusted EBITDA and free cash flow reconciliations, note 35 leases, pension note); 2026 Interim Results for the six months to 30 Jun 2026 (file PSON.L_HalfYear_H2-2026.txt: condensed balance sheet, net debt note, dilution, buyback note, 2026 guidance summary)
data_sources.qualitative: FY2025 Annual Report strategic report and business-unit review; 2026 Interim Results outlook; Pearson pre-close aide memoires dated 30 Mar, 26 Jun and 3 Sep 2026 (Q1 trading update, interim transcript extracts incl. AI skills verification agreement, ELL guidance change, share-count and bond disclosures); 'Introduction to Pearson' May 2026 presentation (medium-term guidance, capital allocation). PSON.L_Analysis.json not yet available at build time.

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Annual Report consolidated cash flow statement, 'Share-based payment costs' GBP39m (2024: 44, 2023: 40). Pearson publishes no combined SBC-plus-equity-tax figure. The GBP72m 'Settlement of share-based payments' in financing (2024: 40) is cash spent buying shares to satisfy vesting awards -- the buyback-like mechanism that keeps the count flat -- so it is NOT added on top of the P&L charge (that would charge dilution twice). Equity-settled transactions are presented net of withholding tax in equity; the withholding element is inside the 72 and not separately disclosed.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025: GBP352m buyback (c.35m shares). H1 FY2026: a further GBP350m programme announced 21 Jan 2026 and COMPLETED in May 2026 at an average 998p (c.35m shares, GBP352m cash). No programme is running at the valuation date; the next is normally announced with FY results in Feb/Mar. Count is held flat because SBC is fully expensed; buybacks are value-neutral in this model and the flat count is being funded by a serial repurchaser (GBP1.7bn returned 2020-25).
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in GBP millions; LSE quote in pence (GBp). fx_rate 100 is the definitional GBP->GBp conversion, not a market rate, so it cannot go stale. Parity reference: PSO (NYSE ADR, 1 ADS = 1 ordinary share) trades at the GBp price / 100 x GBPUSD; not fetched because the conversion is arithmetic.
inputs.share_count_basis: 599m ordinary shares outstanding excluding treasury at 30 Jun 2026 (2026 Interim Results presentation) + 6.1m dilutive share options (H1 FY2026 interim, note 5) = 605.1m fully diluted. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows, so diluting the count as well would double-count. No non-SBC issuance is planned.
inputs.net_debt_basis: Borrowings GBP1,687m non-current + GBP70m current = GBP1,757m less cash GBP339m at 30 Jun 2026 (H1 FY2026 condensed balance sheet). Lease liabilities (GBP478m at FY2025) are EXCLUDED because lease cash is charged inside the flows (treatment B). Pearson's own reported net debt is GBP1,343m: it additionally nets a GBP66m finance-lease (sub-lease) receivable and GBP18m of hedging derivatives; both are left out here so the stripped sub-lease income and its asset stay matched (adaptations rule d). Net debt / adjusted EBITDA 1.3x at FY2025; Pearson caps itself at 2x.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in GBP, the currency of the flows: UK 10-year gilt c.4.5% (Oct 2026) + 0.8 beta x 5.0% ERP = c.8.5% cost of equity; pre-tax cost of debt c.6% (Apr-2026 GBP350m 6.375% notes; older bonds cheaper), c.4.5% after 25% tax; c.15% debt weight at market values (EV c.GBP9.2bn) -> c.7.9%. Rounded to 8.0% and used in ALL THREE scenarios: cyclicality, AI-substitution and contract risk are priced in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked into the discount rate (risk charged once).
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) Leases as operating cost. The full lease payment -- principal GBP77m (financing, 'Repayment of lease liabilities') + interest GBP20m (operating, 'Interest on lease liabilities') = GBP97m, 2.7% of FY2025 revenue -- is charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path, and lease liabilities are excluded from net debt. D&A used for the tax shield is ex right-of-use depreciation (GBP34m): total depreciation 74 + software amortisation 112 + product-development amortisation ex the GBP87m one-off impairment 277 = GBP429m (12.0%). Check: EBITDA 1,116 - SBC 39 - lease 97 - D&A 429 = 551 = adjusted operating profit 614 - (lease cash 97 - ROU depreciation 34). Historical owner FCF deducts lease principal (lease interest is already inside IFRS operating cash flow).
inputs.ebitda_definition: Engine EBITDA is pre-SBC and pre-ALL amortisation of Pearson's own capitalised spend: adjusted operating profit 614 + SBC 39 + depreciation (PPE incl. ROU) 74 + software amortisation 112 + product-development amortisation 277 (364 less the 87 one-off impairment) = GBP1,116m = 31.2% of FY2025 revenue. Pearson's published 'adjusted EBITDA' (GBP800m, 22.4%) adds back only depreciation and software amortisation, treating product-development amortisation as an operating cost; the engine instead charges the actual cash (product development GBP285m is classified by Pearson inside operating cash flow) through capex_pct_path (285 + PPE 29 + software 105 = 419 = 11.7%), so D&A and capex are on the same basis. Acquired-intangible amortisation (GBP41m) is excluded from both EBITDA and D&A: it is non-cash and its 'capex' is M&A, which is not modelled.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated (NCI share of profit is c.GBP1m/yr); the GBP16m book NCI at 30 Jun 2026 is deducted once in the equity bridge.
inputs.pension_note: Net retirement benefit asset GBP482m at FY2025 (UK plan surplus GBP506m less US/other obligations), GBP475m at 30 Jun 2026. NOT added to the bridge: a UK surplus is only accessible via a refund taxed at 25% or a contribution holiday on a closed scheme, and Pearson has indicated no plan to extract it. Potential upside c.GBP360m after tax, c.60p/share, noted in the bull narrative rather than valued.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 2: non-US operating company; owner-fcf.md plus owner-fcf-adaptations.md read in full). Fresh build -- no prior DCF, no memory entry. Pearson is a diversified education company (Assessment & Qualifications 45% of FY2025 sales, Higher Education 22%, Virtual Learning 14%, English Language Learning 11%, Enterprise Learning & Skills 8%); c.60% of revenue is USD, so GBP-reported growth is underlying growth less USD translation (guidance is set at GBP:USD 1.35; 30 Jun 2026 rate 1.32; every 1c = c.GBP5m adjusted operating profit). FY2026 guidance (reiterated 31 Jul 2026): mid-single-digit underlying revenue growth, adjusted operating profit GBP640-685m (includes c.GBP15m/yr lower amortisation after the 2025 product-development impairment), adjusted net finance costs c.GBP80m, adjusted ETR c.25%, FCF conversion 90-100% of adjusted earnings; ELL guidance softened at the interim (PTE declining, return to growth in Q4). Medium-term guidance: mid-single-digit underlying sales CAGR, +40bps adjusted operating margin per year on average, 90-100% FCF conversion. FY2025 reported FCF was flattered by a GBP97m HMRC State Aid tax refund (cash tax paid GBP2m vs c.GBP100-120m normal) and depressed by a c.GBP100m working-capital outflow that reversed in H1 FY2026; neither is carried forward -- the component build uses a 22%->25% cash tax ramp and zero working-capital capture. last_fcf 406 = reported 522 (IFRS OCF 656 - capex 134) - SBC 39 - lease principal 77; interest income is not stripped because Pearson is a net debtor (the engine's flows are unlevered in any case). Nine-month trading update due 22 Oct 2026 -- the first evidence that would move the FY2026 year. Analysis.json was not yet present at build time (qualitative-analyst running in parallel); scenario axes were drawn from the FY2025 annual report, the H1 FY2026 interim (file labelled H2-2026) and the pre-close aide memoires.

bear.rationale: Growth stalls at c.1% as generative AI erodes Higher Education courseware and study-tool pricing, PTE stays in structural decline on tighter migration policy, and A&Q loses a large US state contract on renewal; margins give back c.120bps as Pearson keeps spending c.12% of sales on product and AI to defend share without the revenue to lever it. Terminal growth 1% and a 12x cap reflect a structurally ex-growth publisher multiple. WACC unchanged (risk charged once, in the flows).

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +3.0% headline = mid-single-digit underlying (H1 +4%) less c.1pt USD translation at 1.32-1.34 vs the 1.35 guidance rate. FY2027-29 4.0% = the middle of mid-single-digit guidance, which Pearson has delivered three years running; fades to 2.5% by year 10 as a mature, GDP-plus education franchise.
base.margin_rationale: FY2025 engine EBITDA 31.2%. +40bps in FY2026 (guidance midpoint GBP662m is +80bps on adjusted operating margin, of which c.40bps is lower amortisation, i.e. D&A not EBITDA) then +40bps/yr per medium-term guidance to year 5, slowing to +20-30bps and flat from year 8 at 34.0% (adjusted operating margin c.20%).
base.tax_rationale: Cash tax on EBIT: FY2026 22% (H1 FY2026 paid GBP50m on c.GBP250m EBIT; discrete US-insurance tax benefit in H1), ramping to the guided c.25% adjusted ETR by year 3. The FY2025 GBP2m cash tax (GBP97m State Aid refund) is NOT a base.
base.capex_rationale: Product development 285 + PPE 29 + software 105 = 419 = 11.7% of FY2025 revenue, held, drifting to 11.5% as platform convergence completes; D&A ex-ROU starts at 11.6% (12.0% less the c.GBP15m/yr impairment-related amortisation drop) and converges on capex.

bull.rationale: Upper end of guidance: 5-5.5% underlying growth sustained into the 2030s by Enterprise/AI skills verification scaling, VL enrolment momentum and HE returning to steady growth; +60bps/yr margin as a unified operating company with AI-driven authoring and assessment cost-out; capex intensity eases as platforms converge. Same WACC and cap multiple as base so the scenario is rewarded only through its flows.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 house default to 25/50/25. Bear raised to 25%: AI substitution of courseware and the structural PTE decline are live, two-sided uncertainties on 33% of sales, and ELL guidance was already softened at the July interim; there is no solvency component, which is why it is not higher. Bull cut to 25%: it needs several independent things to go right at once (enterprise AI-certification scaling, HE sustaining growth, PTE recovery, 60bps/yr margin), and the shares have already re-rated c.45% in twelve months on the AI-skills narrative, so the base case already embeds part of what used to be the bull.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
